subject: Post-call recap: Function-calling & structured-output requirements
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@paybridge.io>, Marcus Zhao <m.zhao@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: Function-calling & structured-output requirements

Hi Elena / Marcus — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a shared checklist and next steps. Short version first, details below.

Key pain points you shared:
- Current pipeline: production prompts are brittle when the model emits free-form text; downstream systems must parse and fail when format deviates.
- Operator burden: engineering spends cycles fixing parsing edge-cases and running manual QA on outputs.
- Latency variability: bursty requests plus current batching strategy creates occasional tail latency spikes.

Goals you want to achieve in the next 90 days:
1) Deterministic structured outputs for core actions (payment_authorize, refund_initiate, risk_flag) using a JSON schema contract.
2) A gated rollout path for the schema (canary -> expand) and automated regression detection on schema violations.
3) Proof of concept with production-like traffic (approx 350 rps peak; median payload ~700 tokens) to validate latency and success criteria.

Success criteria we discussed (proposed):
- Schema compliance: >= 99.5% of generated responses validate against the canonical JSON schema for the core actions.
- Determinism: For canonical test prompts, model response token-level variance < 0.2 (measured across fixed seed runs).
- Latency: P50 <= 120ms, P95 <= 350ms under 350 rps with Redwood Dedicated config.
- Error budget: schema violations + parsing failures <= 0.5% over a 7-day rolling window.

Technical notes from call:
- You currently have a microservice that ingests model output and maps it into internal event types. That service is the primary consumer of the structured payloads.
- Desired approach: function-calls where model returns a deterministic JSON payload that maps 1:1 to your event schema. If model cannot satisfy the schema, fallback policy should return a compact error object (error_code, reason, original_text).
- We recommended embedding a small validation layer client-side (lightweight JSON schema check) and server-side metrics that log schema violations, sample payloads, and full tokens for debugging.

Attachments included:
- paybridge-current-prompt-stack.pdf (short deck you shared)
- schema-proposal-v1.json (Redwood suggested canonical schema for payment_authorize + error object)

Next steps (owner & ETA):
- Elena: Share any existing canonical field names / enums we must honor (e.g., currency codes, internal product codes). ETA: EOD Wed (2026-12-02).
- Jordan: Produce a short validation harness (unit tests + small dataset) and a suggested canary rollout plan for Dedicated. Deliverable: validation_harness.zip + rollout_notes.docx. ETA: Fri (2026-12-04).
- Ben: Draft SLOs/expected infra sizing for 350 rps peak and Canary buffer. ETA: Thu (2026-12-03).
- All: Schedule a 30-minute follow-up to finalize schema and runbook. Proposed slot: Tue 2026-12-08 10:00-10:30 PT.

Questions I had after the call:
1) Do you have existing golden prompts and negative test cases we can import?
2) Are there any regulatory constraints on storing full token logs (we can redact user PII if required)?

If that looks right, I'll get the validation harness started and upload a first-pass test report by end of day Friday.

Thanks — Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment stubs:
- schema-proposal-v1.json (attached)
- paybridge-current-prompt-stack.pdf (attached)

From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@paybridge.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Zhao <m.zhao@finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Function-calling & structured-output requirements

Hi Jordan — that summary is perfect, thank you. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- We do have a set of golden prompts (~120) used in internal QA; I'll upload a CSV by Wednesday.
- For enums: product_code values are internal strings (e.g., PB_BASIC, PB_PLUS). We can share the mapping.
- Token logs: we can store full token logs for debug in a restricted S3 bucket; compliance needs an approval chain but should be ok with minimal retention (30 days).

Schema comment: I scanned schema-proposal-v1.json and noticed the payment_authorize object doesn't include an optional metadata->partner_id field we use for marketplace flows. Could you add that?

I'll take the proposed follow-up slot (12/08 10:00 PT). Please send a calendar invite.

Thanks — Elena

--
Elena Soto
Head of Product, PayBridge
elena.soto@paybridge.io | +1 (212) 555-0199

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@paybridge.io>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 13:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Function-calling & structured-output requirements

Elena — adding a couple practical items from engineering/ops perspective:

Proposed deterministic test harness (for POC):
- Ingest your 120 golden prompts + 30 negative cases.
- Run 10 replicates of each prompt through a pinned model variant (quantized) in Redwood Dedicated with a fixed seed.
- Validate output against schema-proposal-v1.json + extended metadata.partner_id field.
- Produce a daily report: schema_validation_rate, sample failing payloads (anonymized), latency histogram, and cost per 1k tokens.

Rollout idea:
- Canary group: 5% of production traffic routed to the new schema pipeline with strict validation. Failures route to the existing free-form flow + alerting channel.
- If schema_validation_rate >= 99.5% for 48 hours, expand to 25% then 100% over a week.

SLO / infra sizing (initial):
- For 350 rps peak, recommend 4x dedicated GPU workers with autoscale headroom to 6x. Estimated cost delta: ~+$9k/mo for Dedicated compared to current managed endpoints; will refine after we run a 24 hr load test.

Jordan — happy to own the validation harness and the first load test. I'll post a draft report into the Drive link once ready.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0087

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Function-calling & structured-output requirements

Thanks Jordan and Ben — this is very actionable. I accepted the calendar invite you sent (12/08 10:00 PT). Two small asks before then:

1) Jordan: Please add the partner_id field to the schema-proposal and upload v1.1 so we can run an internal pass on the CSV.
2) Ben: When you run the 10x replications, can you also include a nightly job that records any minor schema deviations (e.g., missing optional fields) as separate counts? That will help us prioritize fixes.

I'll upload the golden prompts CSV and the product_code mapping by Wednesday EOD. If anything else comes up I'll ping here.

Elena

--
Elena Soto
Head of Product, PayBridge
